alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF, with screening for signs such as changed urine volume. Creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL within 10 weeks of starting TDF, and eGFR is 78. TDF is a known cause of renal toxicity including chronic kidney disease and Fanconi syndrome. Pregnancy itself increases renal blood flow and normally lowers creatinine, making this rise more concerning. The patient has no oedema and urinalysis is normal, which argues against overt TDF nephrotoxicity. However, the upward trend warrants close monitoring. Phosphate is normal, providing some reassurance against Fanconi syndrome.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat serum creatinine and eGFR within 4–6 weeks. Monitor for proteinuria and urinary phosphate. Consider TDF dose review or alternative if creatinine continues rising.

alerts.title: No baseline or follow-up RBS on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines note that hyperglycemia among previously non-diabetic adults has been reported with DTG, and recommend performing random blood sugar every 3 months for high-risk patients during the first 12 months. This patient has no recorded baseline or follow-up blood glucose since initiating DTG 10 weeks ago. Pregnancy itself increases insulin resistance, compounding any DTG-related hyperglycemia risk. No diabetes history is documented, but no screening has been performed to detect new-onset hyperglycemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform a random blood sugar now and repeat every 3 months during the first 12 months of DTG therapy, especially given pregnancy.

alerts.title: Viral load drawn before 6-month schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines state that treatment should be monitored by measuring viral load 6 months after ART initiation and every 6–12 months thereafter. This patient's viral load was drawn at 10 weeks, earlier than the recommended 6-month interval. The result of 89 copies/mL is encouraging but does not replace the scheduled 6-month viral load. A repeat viral load at 6 months is still required per guideline.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule a repeat viral load at 6 months after ART initiation per guideline, regardless of the early result.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Guidelines require screening for developing signs and symptoms at follow-up for patients on TDF and DTG, including renal function monitoring and hyperglycemia screening. The patient has a rising creatinine trend and no blood glucose screening, both of which require actionable plans. Documentation of the plan ensures guideline-recommended monitoring and safety assessments are addressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a plan addressing renal function monitoring, random blood sugar screening, and scheduled 6-month viral load per guidelines.
